author: reek
body: verify-tbs is again the decisive line. The signature is checked over xc-tbs -- the bytes the parser sliced out and kept -- so a parser that re-encoded the tbsCertificate, or took one byte too many, produces a message nobody signed and Ed25519 says False.

author: reek
body: Every line reaches into the parsed certificate through a when, so a failed parse reports itself rather than defaulting to something that looks like a pass.

author: reek
body: The 10.2 certificate is self-issued: its issuer and its subject are the same Name. Compared as raw DER bytes, which is the only comparison that is safe.

author: reek
body: A truncated certificate must not parse. It must not parse PARTIALLY either -- there is no such thing as most of a certificate.
